result.summary: Independently verified lib/letflow/design/req019-tenant-realm-binding.md in full against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-019 (exactly 4 acceptance criteria, description, depends_on: [REQ-015]), REQ-015's tenants schema entry, and REQ-018's entry. All 4 acceptance criteria have concrete, unambiguous design elements: (1) resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and resolve_realm_by_tenant/1 fully specced in §5 with exact @spec, query mechanism, and error shape; (2) one-to-one binding enforcement in §3.2 via unique_constraint(:idp_realm_id, name: :tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index) surfacing REQ-015's existing partial index -- index name independently verified character-for-character against priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs line 40 (exact match); (3) idp_realm_id immutability in §3.3 via structural omission from update_changeset/2's cast/3 list, moduledoc-disclosure instruction given explicitly in §10; (4) verify_realm_ownership/2 guard fully specced in §6 with @spec and all four edge cases (match/mismatch/tenant-not-found/nil-realm) stated exactly, each with its own error atom and reasoning. No TBD/deferral language found anywhere in the design. All function signatures (create_changeset/3, update_changeset/2, resolve_tenant_by_realm/1, resolve_realm_by_tenant/1, verify_realm_ownership/2) carry full @spec input/output/error-tag detail; all error shapes are explicit {:ok,_}|{:error, atom} or Ecto.Changeset.t() tags, none implicit. Cross-module dependencies independently re-derived, not trusted from the design's own claims: read lib/letflow/identity.ex directly and confirmed provision_oidc_user/3's real signature, and confirmed provisioning_error() already contains :realm_tenant_mismatch unused by any function body; read lib/letflow/design/req018-jit-provisioning.md directly (line ~617) and confirmed it explicitly reserves :realm_tenant_mismatch for REQ-019/021 as 'NOT produced by any code path in this design' -- the design's reuse of this atom for the guard's mismatch/nil-realm cases is genuinely the same reserved atom for the same realm-vs-tenant-ownership concept, not a coincidental name collision. Grepped the design file directly for defmodule/def .../case ... do patterns: zero matches; all 12 code fences in the file are @spec-only signature blocks (lines 203-205, 234-237, 269-271, 362-365, 391-394, 421-424), no real function bodies. Independently confirmed no priv/repo/seeds.exs exists anywhere and no .ex/.exs file references a default-tenant row or DEFAULT_TENANT constant (only realm-string config usages of the literal 'bpm-default' exist, in config/dev.exs, config/test.exs, and two REQ-017/018 test files) -- the design's §4 claim about what 'seeded with the default tenant' operationally means (a TEST-DESIGNER-constructed fixture, explicitly not a claimed-to-exist seed) is accurate, not glossed over. The realm-ownership guard's @spec, all four edge cases, and its required call-order before REQ-018's provision_oidc_user/3 (§6.3, explicit pipeline ordering with REQ-021's description cross-checked) are all stated unambiguously. Reviewed all 6 open questions (§8): none affect the correctness of the security-relevant guard logic itself (verify_realm_ownership/2's 4 edge cases are fully resolved with no open question attached) -- all 6 are genuinely deferrable (config-key sourcing, a non-cited mutability judgment call, an out-of-scope seed-file follow-up, a cross-requirement-consistent DB-exception policy, a disclosed-and-justified divergence flagged for awareness not decision, and a future rename left to REQ-021). No FAIL conditions found on any of the 9 checks.
